entries.question: [R-LENS-03]'s LENS_REGISTRY is a CLOSED enumeration keyed on the lessons register's own class list, and a study must map into one of its thirteen rows to publish a lens record. SAVOLA — food manufacturing, grocery retail and a listed quick-service stake — maps to none of them, and BOTH available routes are barred by rules this house already holds. Adding a row is barred because the rule says in terms that a class is added when a DIFFERENT LENS carries the weight and never merely when the industry differs, and a grocer's lens set is identical to three rows already there (primary cash flow; cross-checks own-history EV/EBITDA, a relative multiple and book). Mapping it to one of those rows is barred because a name resolving to the wrong subject is worse than an absence — calling a supermarket group a telecom operator would put that label in the study's own record. So SAVOLA cannot retire its typed 45/25/15/15 blend under [R-LENS-03] without one of the two being decided.

routes.outcome: 13 classes; three rows (telecom operator, airline, pharmaceutical manufacturer) carry an IDENTICAL lens set. The duplication is the evidence: the registry keys on an industry NAME while the thing it stores is a lens SET.

routes.outcome: IT IS THE GROUP'S, and the group is larger than anyone had counted. All SEVEN studies invisible to [R-GAP-01] are invisible for this exact reason: each publishes a multi-lens combination [R-LENS-03] retired and therefore no single central. AND FOUR OF THE SEVEN MEET THE SAME WALL AS SAVOLA AND EMPOWER: fuel retail, restaurants, offshore drilling and cable manufacturing are in no row of the registry, and none of them is a DIFFERENT LENS — every one is a cash-flow primary with a relative multiple and book beside it. So the count of names this gap blocks is now NINE, not two, and eight of them cannot publish a readable answer until it is settled.

routes.route: GBCO's own delivered document and committed numbers, opened rather than inferred — the one name of the nine the count had placed on the OTHER side
routes.outcome: IT IS THE FIFTH INSTANCE, NOT ONE OF THE THREE THAT CAN PROCEED, and it is the SHARPEST case for the default fix rather than a complication of it. The 5-Sep count above put GBCO among the three studies with a registered class; its own masthead and section 1.1 say otherwise in terms — 'we value GB Corp as an operating company with a captive finance arm and split the legs', primary lens 'split-the-legs sum-of-the-parts (operating company + captive lender)'. THERE IS NO ROW FOR THAT. What makes it the sharpest case is what happens next: the registry's holding-company row stores EXACTLY the lens set GBCO needs — an SOTP primary with a relative multiple and book beside it — so the registry already contains the right answer and refuses it on the ROW'S NAME ALONE. GB Corp is not a holding company by the rule's own test (a holdco IS its stakes; this is an auto assembler-distributor with a captive lender and one large associate), and filing it as one would put that label in its committed record, which is the 'wrong subject is worse than an absence' bar. Under the default fix — rows named for their lens sets — GBCO maps with nobody inventing a fit, exactly as SAVOLA does. So the affected count is FIVE of the seven unreadable studies and NINE names in total, and the only one of the seven that can take the lever today is STC (telecom operator, a row that exists).

Four of those are now readable and audited, and every one of the four reviews reaches the same verdict: the gap is OURS and the single largest correction is retiring the typed multi-lens blend under [R-LENS-03]. NONE OF THE FOUR CAN TAKE IT. So the delay now blocks the largest identified correction on four audited studies simultaneously, and on two of them it blocks a correction that would move the answer AWAY from the price, which is the shape that proves the answer is not being chosen for where it lands.

entries.default_if_no_answer: RENAME THE REGISTRY'S ROWS FOR THEIR LENS SETS RATHER THAN FOR INDUSTRIES, and merge the three duplicates into one row — an operating company valued on its own cash flows and cross-checked on its own EV/EBITDA history, a relative multiple and book. entries.note: The gap is worth naming beyond this one name: the registry is keyed on an industry NAME and stores a lens SET, and three of its thirteen rows already store the same set. A taxonomy that must grow per industry, under a rule that forbids growing per industry, has no state in which a new operating company can be added — which is a property of the design rather than of any study that meets it. EMPOWER adds one thing the first instance could not show: its blend carries a NORMALISED EARNINGS lens at 15%, and normalised earnings appears in no row of the registry at all. So even under the default fix — rename the rows for their lens sets and merge the duplicates — that lens still has to go, which is the rule working as intended rather than a further gap in it. [5-Sep-2026] The evidence has widened from two names to nine and the shape has not changed, which is what makes the default fix look right rather than expedient: not one of the seven added today needs a lens the registry lacks — they need a ROW WHOSE NAME IS NOT AN INDUSTRY. And the cost of the delay is now measurable in a second currency: these seven are exactly the studies the valuation-gap gate can say nothing about, so a taxonomy question is holding a PUBLICATION gate blind over a third of the book. [5-Sep-2026, second reading] GBCO was counted on the wrong side of this wall for a day and the correction matters twice over. It raises the blocked count from four of the seven to five, and it supplies the case that settles the DESIGN question rather than adding another instance of it: every earlier name needed a row whose NAME is not an industry while the LENS SET was already there three times over; GBCO needs a row whose name is not an industry while the lens set is there ONCE, under a name that is a real and different subject. A taxonomy keyed on industry cannot express 'an operating company valued on its parts' without either inventing a class for every industry that is one, or calling an auto assembler a holding company. THE OBSERVATION THAT WAS MISSED IS ALSO WORTH KEEPING: this session asserted GBCO could proceed and wrote it into the programme state before opening GBCO's own document, which is L-334 and L-335 for the sixth time in one session.

entries.done_meanwhile: Nothing is blocked and nothing was invented. The 2015 and 2016 origins are DROPPED with their stated reason, which is the correct output — [R-FCAL-01] says leave the year out and shorten the window rather than interpolate, and deriving capex across 2013 to 2015 would present a two-year change as one year's spending. The comparable gap on PHDC, where that company's own filing for the missing year IS legible, is being carried instead, so the recoverable cells are being recovered.
entries.default_if_no_answer: The two origins stay dropped and the mechanical series is scored on the cells that exist. The window shortens; nothing is fabricated.
entries.recommendation: Supply a legible copy if one exists; otherwise accept the shortened window. Two cells are worth having and neither is worth inventing, and the cost of the absence is already visible in criterion 3's own drop list, which is where a reader would look.

entries.question: Two joined questions about [R-VCAL-01] series (a). (1) score_cashflow.py writes to a HARDCODED filename, SCORES_cashflow_06-09-2026.json, so re-running it OVERWRITES a file whose own name states a date the contents would no longer be from — a stale stamp of exactly the kind this house refuses elsewhere. (2) Two valuation-input carries landed today (PHDC's FY2022, ARCC's FY2015-16) and the scorer has not been re-run, so criterion3's printed verdict still reads the 6 September file. Does the principal want the scorer re-run now, and the output dated by its run rather than by a literal?

routes.route: score_cashflow.py read end to end, and its pre-registration
routes.outcome: the scorer chooses NOTHING at run time — statistics, blocks, seed, eras and the four printed readings are all fixed in the sealed declaration. So re-running it is not a decision about the method; it is the method being applied to more data. The only thing in the way is the filename.

routes.route: scripts/check_valuation_calibration.py, to see whether a NEW dated score file would satisfy the commit-topology rule
routes.outcome: it globs any file carrying a score marker and requires the pre-registration's introducing commit to be an ANCESTOR of each score file's. A new file written today satisfies that; the constraint is not what blocks this.

routes.route: the two carries' own in-memory re-runs of cashflow_lens against the tree as it now stands, which is the question re-scoring would answer
routes.outcome: ANSWERED, and it is why this is not urgent. PHDC's carry takes 5 scored cells to 6 and populates a second era; ARCC's clears all three of its capex-intensity drops, which then land on TERMINAL refusals the sanctioned module is right to make. The series stays on ONE name, clause A's pooled mean moves +0.9842 to +1.0439 and still excludes zero at every block length, and CRITERION 3 REMAINS NOT MET. Re-scoring tonight would rewrite a dated artefact to print a verdict already known.

entries.why_only_the_principal: Re-dating the output of a sealed, pre-registered calibration is a decision about that programme's own artefact discipline rather than a repair — and doing it unsupervised, to produce a verdict that does not change, is the shape of act this method distrusts. The arithmetic question is already answered; what is left is whose call the naming is.
entries.done_meanwhile: Both carries are committed and their effect is MEASURED and reported rather than assumed. criterion3 prints the stale figure and nothing depends on it: no fair value, no publish, no gate. The drop list it prints is the honest map of what remains.
entries.default_if_no_answer: Leave the 6 September file as it stands and re-score at the next carry, dating the output by its run and resolving it by pattern — so the two changes happen together and neither a literal filename nor a stale stamp survives the change.
entries.recommendation: Re-score, and date the output by the run rather than by a literal, with criterion3 resolving the latest by pattern — the same discipline the digest's own dated file already uses. Not because the verdict moves, but because the carries are real work and a programme whose printed verdict silently lags its own inputs will lag them again next time, and nobody will know which run it is reading.
entries.answer: RULED BY THE PRINCIPAL: do not switch the declared maintenance basis. Changing the rule after seeing which answer it produces is selection, which is what the pre-registration exists to prevent. The disclosed-life reading stays a PUBLISHED SENSITIVITY beside the declared run, as designed. The separate filename question stands: when the scorer is next re-run, date its output by the run rather than by a literal.
entries.answer_written_to: engine/valuation_calibration/score_cashflow.py — the declared reading is unchanged and this ruling is why.

entries.question: Palm Hills Development's land bank as at a date no earlier than 31 March 2026 — the figure the company states in its FY2025 and 1Q2026 earnings releases, if it states one. The study registers 33.0 million square metres dated 31 December 2024 from the FY2024 release, and its own information set ends 31 March 2026, so the quantity the whole present-value net asset view is built out of is fifteen months older than the information set. This is the defect [R-ASSET-01] was adopted on, in the principal's own words: a study that takes the current land bank of a developer and does not account for new land added to it.

routes.route: the company's own investor-relations page, www.palmhillsdevelopments.com/investor-relations/, fetched directly
routes.outcome: HTTP 200 and USELESS: the page is JavaScript-rendered and its raw HTML carries 27 links and ZERO pdfs, so nothing on it can be enumerated without executing the page.

routes.route: the same page through the headless browser this environment installs, which is the route that defeats a rendered source
routes.outcome: net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET on navigation, repeatably, while plain curl reaches the same URL — so the block is on the browser's own connection rather than on the host. Reported, not routed around.

routes.route: the apex host without the www prefix, palmhillsdevelopments.com/investors/
routes.outcome: HTTP 525 — a TLS handshake failure at the edge, not a missing page.

routes.route: the study's own committed register, for a later land-bank figure it may already hold
routes.outcome: land_bank_sqm_mn is the ONLY land-bank quantity registered and it is the FY2024 release's. The register names a 1Q2026 earnings release as a source for other figures — exactly the document a developer restates a land bank in — and that release is not committed to this repository, so whether it carries an updated figure is not established from here.

entries.why_only_the_principal: Pure access. The document is published by the issuer and the issuer's site cannot be read from this container by either available route. The principal has supplied primary filings before when a company site refused, and this protocol records that as the rule working rather than failing.
entries.done_meanwhile: The gap is MEASURED and already carried on the asset-base ratchet with its full figures rather than as a bare name, so the debt is countable. A ready-made generator sits in the study directory (asset_base_record.py) which writes the record the moment a sourced figure exists; it is deliberately NOT wired into the build, because running it today commits a record whose only content is that the base is stale, which the ratchet already says in more detail. A record that adds nothing and turns a gate red is not a repair.
entries.default_if_no_answer: Declare not_restated_since ONLY if the FY2025 and 1Q2026 releases can be read and neither restates the land bank — never on the assumption that they do not. Failing that, PHDC stays on the asset-base ratchet and the land bank is flagged in the study's own limitations as a quantity whose vintage the study cannot establish.
entries.note: The resolving marker is a file that does not exist yet, on the ELEC precedent, rather than a field that already does. A first draft keyed this on the land_bank_sqm_mn input, which is present today — so the entry read as already answered the moment it was written, and the escalation gate said so. What has to change is that input's DATE, and no checker can read an intention, so the close is a person writing down where the newer figure came from.

entries.question: Orascom Construction is listed twice — ADX primary in AED (ISIN AEE01702O253) and EGX secondary in EGP (ISIN EGS95001C011), same ticker — and on the sweep date the company's own page quoted both at once, EGP 855.85 against AED 60.30. SIGCM clause 6 says the regressor is the published index of the exchange the stock is LISTED on, and this stock is listed on two. Which exchange does ORAS strike on?

routes.route: engine/raw_ohlc/EG/ORAS.csv held against both quoted prices
routes.outcome: closes 782.25 on 23-08-2026, the EGP magnitude, so the series this repository holds is the EGX line and is correctly filed under EG

routes.route: www.adx.ae and api.adx.ae, for an ADX price series
routes.outcome: HTTP 403 and CONNECT tunnel failed 502 — no ADX series is obtainable here

entries.why_only_the_principal: Not an access problem. Both readings conform to a rule and they disagree: the EGX line is the series held and EGX30 is its conforming regressor, while ADX is where the stock is primarily listed. Picking one is a house judgement about which listing a beta should describe, and market AE deliberately RAISES rather than guessing between ADX and DFM, so nothing in the code would have chosen for us.
entries.done_meanwhile: the sweep closed all four rings without a regressor, and no beta was resolved — which is why this question could be asked before any number depended on it
entries.default_if_no_answer: hold ORAS off the queue rather than strike it on a regressor nobody chose; a beta measured against the wrong index is the FERTIGLB defect, where a non-conforming regressor understated beta by about 40%
entries.note: RULED: strike on EGX against engine/raw_indices/EG/EGX30.csv. The ADX primary listing is disclosed in the study, and so is the fact that the beta is measured on the secondary line. TWO COMPLICATIONS THE BUILD CARRIES: the ADX listing REPLACED Nasdaq Dubai inside the regression window — the January-2025 shareholding disclosure still names AEDFXA14NUL7 — and the pound moved from about 47.6 to about 52 to the dollar across it.

entries.question: Orascom Construction carries a share issue that has NOT completed: 97,201,359 new shares at USD 1 plus USD 12.79 premium, taking issued capital from 110,243,935 to 207,445,294 — up 88.2% — per the shareholders' circular of 8 January 2026. The long stop is 30 December 2026, the OCI vote is pending and a rival all-cash NNS offer at EUR 4.10 is outstanding. A per-share value on either share count alone is a claim about which outcome happens. How is it framed?

routes.route: the Step 2A sweep of 08-09-2026, which reached orascom.com's investor shelf in full and carried the circular's own terms
routes.outcome: the TERMS are established — ratio 0.4634, ORAS equity value USD 1,520.0mn against OCI USD 1,347.9mn, consideration about 47% — and the OUTCOME is not. The sweep recorded it as a base changer to be dual-framed and never smoothed.

entries.why_only_the_principal: The question is not what the terms are but what a study may assert. Blending the two share counts by a probability would state a view on a shareholder vote, and this house publishes distributions rather than views on binary corporate events.
entries.done_meanwhile: the sweep closed and both share counts are registered, so either frame can be built
entries.default_if_no_answer: build standalone only and disclose the event with its terms, valuing nothing that depends on the vote
entries.note: RULED: DUAL-FRAME. The study is built on the standalone company and the combined case is carried as a fully separate valuation with its own share count. Neither is blended into the other and NO PROBABILITY IS APPLIED to the outcome — a weighted single number would be a view on a vote.

entries.question: Alexandria Mineral Oils' total sales tonnage for FY2021-FY2025 by year, and its per-product-line tonnage over the same span. The study prints the annual series as 1,492 / 1,548 / 1,449 / 1,433 / 1,262 thousand tonnes and derives a five-year mean of 1,437 and a base-year annualisation of 1,616 from it. NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CARRIES THAT SERIES. It matters because the BEAR CASE is anchored to it: the volume dial is set at -4.5% a year and its stated purpose is to return tonnage toward that mean.

routes.route: the three committed AMOC filings in engine/amoc_study/filings/
routes.outcome: two December-2025 statements and one June-2025. Note 14-A gives ONE half's tonnage by line with a VALUE-only comparative. Grepped all three for the five annual totals: none present. FY2022-FY2024 per-line tonnage would need filings this study does not hold.

routes.route: engine/amoc_study/filings/AUDITED_EXTRACT.md, the committed extract
routes.outcome: carries note 14-A for the half only; no annual series of any kind

routes.route: the company's own investor-relations shelf, www.amoc.com.eg/en/investor-relations
routes.outcome: curl (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 502 over https; plain http returns 'Could not resolve host: www.amoc.com.eg'. The company site is not reachable from this environment at all, by either scheme.

routes.route: the Egyptian Exchange, www.egx.com.eg/en/HomePage.aspx
routes.outcome: curl (52) Empty reply from server after 1.5s — the same EGX block three other sweeps hit today (ORAS, HRHO and ISPH all logged it). Not a one-off and not this probe's fault.

entries.why_only_the_principal: Pure access to superseded filings. Four earlier annual reports would settle it and none is on disk; SIGCM forbids reconstructing a historical series from a vendor, a press summary or an interpolation, and these are the figures a bear case is anchored to.
entries.done_meanwhile: the four per-line compound rates that rested on the same series are NO LONGER PRINTED — the prose check caught one of the four and the other three were unflagged rather than verified, so under SIGCM a figure this desk cannot source is one it does not print. The DIRECTION survives, which is what the argument needs: six lines down, two up. The bear leg's own description was also corrected in the same pass: it claimed -4.5% a year returns tonnage to the five-year mean by year five, and it does not — it lands at 1,284, BELOW that mean and close to the last audited year. Reaching the mean would need only -2.3% a year. The dial is unchanged and now an assertion checks that the sentence describing it is true.
entries.default_if_no_answer: stop printing the five annual totals, the five-year mean and the base-year annualisation, and re-anchor the bear leg on something this repository holds — which would be a study act with its own ledger entry, not a record fix
